hero.headline: First-time Grand Slam champion to be crowned at French Open
hero.teaser: The men's semifinals in Paris will determine which player wins their first major title.
hero.body:
The French Open is guaranteed to crown a first-time Grand Slam champion this year after the men's and women's semifinals produced four players who have never won a major tournament.

In the men's draw, Flavio Cobolli reached the semifinals after a remarkable comeback victory. The Italian 10th seed defeated fourth-seeded Felix Auger-Aliassime 4-6, 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 in the quarterfinals, recovering from a set and a break down. This was Cobolli's first win against a top 10 opponent at a Grand Slam. His triumph set up an all-Italian men's semifinal for the first time in history, as Matteo Arnaldi also advanced when fellow Italian Matteo Berrettini retired injured.

Cobolli's path through the tournament has been efficient and authoritative. Through five matches, he has conceded just two sets while playing decisive tennis when it matters most. His game combines a destructive forehand with well-rounded skills that have allowed him to neutralize opponents' weapons. Against Auger-Aliassime, Cobolli pinned the Canadian in his backhand corner and narrowed the court with superior defensive abilities after breaking serve at 3-1 in the first set.

The loss represents a significant missed opportunity for Auger-Aliassime, who at 25 has been among the tour's longest-serving players without a major title. The Canadian was the highest-ranked player remaining in his half after Jannik Sinner's early exit, giving him a genuine chance to compete for the championship.

On the women's side, qualifier Maja Chwalinska reached the final with a stunning 7-6, 6-4 victory over 25th seed Diana Shnaider. Chwalinska became the first qualifier ever to reach a Roland Garros final. Her emotional response after the win, sobbing into her towel, reflected the magnitude of her achievement after coming through an extraordinarily difficult period in her life.

The pressure of competing for a first major title will test all four semifinalists in different ways. Cobolli and Arnaldi must navigate their historic matchup while maintaining the form that brought them this far. Chwalinska carries the weight of her journey and the expectations that come with being the first qualifier to reach this final. Her opponent in the women's final will also be pursuing their first Grand Slam title.

The absence of established champions in both semifinals means that Sunday's finals will feature players competing for major titles for the first time in their careers. How each handles the pressure and intensity of that moment could determine who leaves Roland Garros with their name etched into Grand Slam history.

cards.headline: Zelensky proposes direct talks with Putin to end war
cards.teaser: Ukraine's president sent an open letter to Putin calling for face-to-face negotiations, citing reduced US focus as Washington prioritizes Iran.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has called for face-to-face negotiations with Russian President Vladimir Putin in a public letter—the first he has directly addressed to Putin since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. Zelensky argues that only direct engagement between the two countries can end the war.

The letter, which criticized Putin's 26 years in power, proposed holding talks in a neutral third country. The move comes as the United States shifts its foreign policy focus toward Iran, prompting Zelensky's diplomatic outreach.

cards.headline: Israel continues Lebanon strikes as Hezbollah rejects ceasefire plan
cards.teaser: Israeli Prime Minister ordered new attacks on Beirut suburbs as fighting with Hezbollah escalates.
cards.body:
Israel continued its ground operations in southern Lebanon and launched strikes on Beirut suburbs after Hezbollah rejected a ceasefire agreement. The United States announced the ceasefire deal on Wednesday night following fresh rounds of talks.

The conflict has expanded with reports of casualties among international peacekeepers. A UN peacekeeping mission peacekeeper was killed and others were wounded by mortar fire in southeastern Lebanon. The rejection of the ceasefire proposal indicates the conflict will likely persist without immediate signs of de-escalation.

cards.headline: House passes Ukraine aid and Russia sanctions over Trump objections
cards.teaser: The House approved legislation providing aid to Ukraine and imposing sanctions on Russia, breaking with Trump for the second time in a week.
cards.body:
The House voted 226-195 to pass legislation providing aid to Ukraine and imposing sanctions on key Russian economic sectors, defying objections from Republican leaders. The bill represents the chamber's second major foreign policy break with Trump in a week, following a war powers resolution on Iran approved the previous day.

Republican leaders had warned the measure would undermine negotiations they believed could achieve stronger results. Despite this pressure, House Republicans joined Democrats in supporting the Ukraine assistance and Russian sanctions package.

cards.headline: House committee approves $1.15 trillion defense bill after 14-hour debate
cards.teaser: The House Armed Services Committee passed the annual defense policy bill late Thursday, advancing the nearly $1.15 trillion measure to the full House after a ma.
cards.body:
The House Armed Services Committee passed the annual defense policy bill Thursday evening, advancing the $1.15 trillion National Defense Authorization Act to the full House following an intensive 14-hour markup session. The committee voted 44 members in favor after debating approximately 900 proposed amendments to the fiscal 2027 bill.

The NDAA sets military policy and spending priorities across weapons systems, personnel costs, and operational budgets. Congress has passed a defense authorization bill for over 60 consecutive years, typically with bipartisan support. The measure now goes to the full House for debate and votes before moving to the Senate, where it must be reconciled with a Senate version and signed by the president to become law.

cards.headline: Trump directs $700 million to coal industry under wartime authority
cards.body:
President Trump has announced a major investment in the coal industry, framing it as a national security priority during the ongoing conflict with Iran. The funding represents a significant federal intervention in energy markets at a time when fuel prices are affecting American consumers.

During a White House ceremony on Wednesday, Trump signed an executive order directing the Department of Defense to purchase long-term power from coal plants for military installations and other critical facilities. "We're going to be buying a lot of coal through the military now," Trump said at the event, which included coal executives, miners, and Republican lawmakers.

The announcement included an additional allocation of $175 million from the Department of Energy to modernize and extend the operation of coal-fired power plants serving rural communities in West Virginia, Ohio, North Carolina, and Kentucky. The administration framed both initiatives as part of a broader strategy to increase domestic energy production and reduce reliance on foreign oil markets during wartime.

The coal industry has welcomed the support. James Grech, CEO of Peabody Energy, the largest coal company in the United States, praised Trump's actions. "We stand here today representing the thousands of coalminers across the country to express our deep gratitude to you, sir, for the actions you've taken to support our industry," Grech said.

This latest move follows other administration efforts to revive coal. In September, the White House announced $625 million for coal-fired power plants and opened 13.1 million acres of public land to coal mining.

The investment marks a significant policy shift toward fossil fuel production despite long-term industry trends. Coal has experienced sharp decline in recent decades. According to the Energy Information Administration, U.S. coal production in 2023 was less than half its 2008 level, and coal plants generated only about 15 percent of American electricity in 2024, compared to roughly 50 percent in 2000.

Energy analysts note that coal production faces structural challenges that extend beyond current market conditions. Aging infrastructure and competition from cheaper natural gas plants have created persistent headwinds for the industry. The federal investment could provide short-term support to coal producers, but economists question whether it can address the longer-term economic pressures reshaping the energy sector.

Trump stated that the administration aims to position the United States as "a massive energy exporter" and said the government is "lifting up our hard-working American miners like nobody has ever done before." The funding relies on presidential authority typically reserved for national security emergencies, with the administration citing energy supply disruptions from the Iran conflict as justification for the intervention.

cards.headline: Xi Jinping to visit North Korea next week for first time since 2019
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping will travel to North Korea on June 8-9 to meet with leader Kim Jong Un, marking his first visit to the country in five years. The trip occurs just weeks after Xi held separate meetings with the leaders of the United States and Russia, both of whom significantly influence North Korea's foreign policy direction.

The announcement of Xi's journey has drawn considerable attention among foreign policy experts. Satellite imagery had sparked early speculation about the visit before official confirmation came through. The timing suggests China wants to reassert its position in Pyongyang during a period when North Korea has grown closer to Russia in recent years.

Xi will encounter a more independent Kim Jong Un than in previous encounters. North Korea's strengthening alliance with Russia has diminished Pyongyang's traditional reliance on China for economic support and diplomatic backing. This shift has given Kim greater negotiating power with Beijing, which could complicate Xi's efforts to influence North Korean decisions on nuclear weapons and broader regional security matters.

The visit represents an uncommon face-to-face meeting between the two leaders. China has historically been North Korea's main economic supporter and has defended the country at the United Nations, but the relationship has experienced tension as Kim has pursued stronger connections with Moscow. The Russian-North Korean partnership has involved military cooperation and economic dealings that work outside traditional Chinese networks.

Xi's decision to travel to Pyongyang shows China recognizes the need to actively engage with Kim to preserve influence over the Korean Peninsula. The meetings will probably discuss regional security issues, economic partnership opportunities, and the shifting power dynamics in Northeast Asia as the United States, China, and Russia manage an increasingly strained geopolitical situation.

North Korea's emboldened position stems partly from its reduced dependence on Chinese support. As Russia has become a more significant ally, Kim has gained leverage in his dealings with Beijing. This dynamic makes Xi's visit particularly significant, as he attempts to maintain China's role as North Korea's primary international backer during a time of geopolitical realignment.

The visit underscores how the broader competition between major powers continues to reshape relationships across East Asia. China's need to court Kim demonstrates the stakes involved in maintaining regional influence. As these three powers navigate their competing interests, North Korea's position as a strategic actor has become more valuable and more contested than it has been in previous years.

cards.headline: Zelenskyy proposes direct talks with Putin to end Ukraine war
cards.teaser: Ukraine's president sent a letter to his Russian counterpart calling for face-to-face negotiations.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has written an open letter directly to Russian President Vladimir Putin calling for face-to-face negotiations to end the war. The letter, Zelenskyy's first public direct communication to Putin since Russia's 2022 invasion, represents a significant diplomatic shift and includes a sweeping critique of Putin's 26 years in power.

Zelenskyy argues that only direct engagement between Ukraine and Russia can resolve the conflict. The proposal suggests holding talks in a neutral third country. The move comes as international attention has shifted, with the U.S. focused on Iran, potentially creating diplomatic space for bilateral Ukrainian-Russian discussions.

cards.headline: Israel continues Lebanon strikes as Hezbollah rejects ceasefire plan
cards.teaser: Israeli Prime Minister ordered new attacks on Beirut suburbs as fighting with Hezbollah escalates.
cards.body:
Israel continued its ground operations in southern Lebanon and launched strikes on Beirut suburbs after Hezbollah rejected a ceasefire agreement. The United States announced the ceasefire deal on Wednesday night following fresh rounds of talks.

The conflict has expanded with reports of casualties among international peacekeepers. A UN peacekeeping mission peacekeeper was killed and others were wounded by mortar fire in southeastern Lebanon. The rejection of the ceasefire proposal indicates the conflict will likely persist without immediate signs of de-escalation.

cards.headline: Oman oil terminal disrupted after reported explosion
cards.teaser: The Mina al Fahal terminal delayed loadings, though Oman said operations remain normal.
cards.body:
Oman's Mina al Fahal oil terminal experienced loading suspensions following reports of an explosion, according to oil traders. The disruption at this major export facility contributed to rising crude oil prices as markets responded to concerns about potential supply constraints in a region already dealing with heightened Iran-related tensions.

Omani authorities stated that terminal operations were proceeding normally despite trader reports of suspended loadings. The facility handles a significant share of Oman's oil exports.

cards.headline: Sherpa guide found alive on Everest after week missing
cards.teaser: Hillary Dawa Sherpa survived six days alone on Mount Everest and was rescued while crawling toward base camp.
cards.body:
A Sherpa guide missing on Mount Everest was discovered alive after six days alone on the mountain. Hillary Dawa Sherpa was spotted by cleaners as he crawled toward Base Camp, having survived extreme conditions at high altitude without supplies or support.

The discovery came as a surprise to his family, who had already begun funeral rites. Climber Chris Thrall, who was with Dawa Sherpa when they became separated, recounted the moment they lost each other on the mountain. The rescue stands out as a rare survival story from one of the world's deadliest peaks.

cards.headline: Dubai ruler's nephew's ex-wife in custody
cards.teaser: Zeynab Javadli has not been in contact with friends since earlier this week, prosecutors confirm.
cards.body:
The ex-wife of the nephew of Dubai's ruler is in custody, according to prosecutors. Zeynab Javadli had not been in contact with any of her friends since Tuesday, raising concerns about her whereabouts before authorities confirmed her detention.

Prosecutors provided no additional information about the reasons for her custody or what charges, if any, she may face. The case has drawn attention given the high-profile nature of the family connections involved.

cards.headline: Australian authorities seize 100,000 illegal cockroaches
cards.teaser: A record insect bust uncovered a massive cache of prohibited insects in Australia.
cards.body:
Australian authorities arrested a person they described as a cockroach kingpin after discovering 100,000 illegal insects. The seizure represents the largest illegal insect bust on record in the country, where strict biosecurity laws regulate the import and possession of non-native species.

The case highlights Australia's efforts to prevent the introduction of foreign insects that could threaten native ecosystems or agriculture. Authorities did not disclose what the insects were intended for or how they were being stored.

hero.headline: Los Angeles mayoral race tightens as new ballots narrow Bass lead
hero.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass saw her lead shrink as election officials continued counting ballots in the city's mayoral primary. Challenger Nithya Raman gained ground on Bass, though many ballots remain uncounted in the race.

Bass thanked supporters and predicted she would win a second term despite the tightening margin. The race has drawn national attention as one of several high-profile municipal contests in California this year.

Raman, who represents areas stretching from the San Fernando Valley to Silver Lake on the Los Angeles City Council, entered the mayoral race just hours before the filing deadline. During her campaign announcement, she outlined concerns about the city's direction, stating that "Los Angeles is at a breaking point, and people feel it in the most basic ways."

Raman focused her campaign on several key issues. She criticized housing costs that are "forcing families out of the city" and called attention to what she described as a homelessness system "that lacks clear ownership and accountability." She also emphasized public safety concerns, noting that "too many people don't feel safe walking down their own blocks at night," even as overall crime has declined.

Throughout her tenure on the city council, Raman has concentrated on rent stabilization and efforts to address homelessness. She has also connected with leaders in the housing advocacy movement, supporting measures to expand housing production through strategies like upzoning single-family neighborhoods.

The race comes after a volatile filing period for the Los Angeles mayoral contest. County Supervisor Lindsey Horvath decided not to enter the race, choosing instead to focus on her reelection bid for the county board of supervisors. Her decision came one day before the filing deadline. Earlier in the week, former Los Angeles Unified School District Superintendent Austin Beutner and developer Rick Caruso also announced they would not be running.

Bass, who previously served in Congress, won her first term as mayor in 2022. Her record has faced scrutiny over her handling of wildfires that burned parts of Los Angeles early last year.

The mayoral race is being conducted amid ongoing immigration enforcement actions by the Trump administration. Bass has characterized these actions as "an attack from our own federal government" and an affront to cities across the country.

California's ballot counting process often extends days or weeks beyond election day as officials verify and tally mail-in and provisional ballots. The state allows ballots postmarked by election day to arrive and be counted for up to a week afterward, with additional time needed to verify signatures and process ballots requiring correction.

Election officials have not announced when they expect to finish counting all ballots. The outcome will determine leadership for the nation's second-largest city as it grapples with housing affordability, homelessness, and public safety concerns.

cards.teaser: The House approved legislation providing aid to Ukraine and imposing sanctions on Russia, breaking with Trump for the second time in a week.

Republican leaders had warned the measure would undermine negotiations they believed could achieve stronger results. Despite this pressure, House Republicans joined Democrats in supporting the Ukraine assistance and Russian sanctions package.

cards.headline: Multiple women allege unsettling behavior by Graham Platner
cards.teaser: Several women who dated Graham Platner have come forward with accounts of unsettling behavior, and new allegations include Nazi tattoo claims.
cards.body:
Graham Platner, a Democratic Senate candidate in Maine, is rejecting allegations detailed in a New York Times report published Thursday. The article includes an interview with a Republican operative who accused him of womanizing, physical misconduct, and making troubling comments about rape.

Platner characterizes the allegations as "politically motivated" and denies claims of physical abuse. He describes the accusations as "simply not true."

cards.headline: Anthropic co-founder calls for ability to slow AI development
cards.teaser: Jack Clark told the BBC that artificial intelligence could reach a point where it develops without human input, raising safety concerns.
cards.body:
Jack Clark, co-founder of artificial intelligence company Anthropic, said regulators and developers need the ability to slow down AI advancement. Speaking to BBC's Newsnight, Clark warned that AI technology could progress to a stage where it develops autonomously, without human guidance.

The comments reflect growing debate within the tech industry about AI safety and oversight. Anthropic, a San Francisco-based company, focuses on developing AI systems with safety features built in from the start.

cards.headline: Putin announces plans to strengthen air defenses after Ukrainian drone strikes
cards.teaser: The Russian president said his country will bolster air defense systems in response to Ukrainian drone attacks that have reached deep into Russia.
cards.body:
President Vladimir Putin announced that Russia will strengthen its air defense systems in response to Ukrainian drone attacks penetrating deep into Russian territory. The strikes have reached areas far from the Ukrainian border, including incidents during Putin's economic forum in St. Petersburg, creating uncertainty around the high-profile event.

Ukraine's President Zelensky has proposed direct face-to-face talks with Putin, arguing that only direct engagement between the two countries can end the war. The proposal comes as the US focuses its diplomatic efforts on Iran rather than the Ukraine conflict.

cards.headline: Zelensky proposes direct talks with Putin to end war
cards.teaser: Ukraine's president sent an open letter to Putin calling for face-to-face negotiations, citing reduced US focus as Washington prioritizes Iran.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has called for face-to-face negotiations with Russian President Vladimir Putin in a public letter—the first he has directly addressed to Putin since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. Zelensky argues that only direct engagement between the two countries can end the war.

The letter, which criticized Putin's 26 years in power, proposed holding talks in a neutral third country. The move comes as the United States shifts its foreign policy focus toward Iran, prompting Zelensky's diplomatic outreach.

cards.headline: UK military chief warns of most dangerous security period in memory
cards.teaser: Chief of the Defence Staff Sir Richard Knighton said Russian incursions into UK defenses risk crossing a line.
cards.body:
Britain's Chief of the Defence Staff Sir Richard Knighton has warned that the UK faces its most dangerous security period in his experience. He told the BBC that Russian incursions probing UK defences risk crossing a line that could trigger wider conflict.

His comments reflect growing tensions between NATO countries and Russia, highlighting concerns about the potential for military escalation in the region.

cards.headline: SpaceX sets up website for retail investors ahead of $75 billion IPO
cards.teaser: The company is preparing for what would be the largest initial public offering in history.
cards.body:
SpaceX has launched a dedicated website for retail investors as it prepares for a public offering seeking $75 billion next week. The company has told banks it will not adjust its proposed share price of $135, according to reports.

Jamie Dimon is planning to personally pitch investors on the offering. Index funds are preparing to allocate space for SpaceX shares, though S&P confirmed it will not change existing rules to allow early entry into its benchmark index. The IPO is generating significant interest among traders and institutional investors.

cards.headline: S&P denies SpaceX early entry to benchmark index
cards.teaser: The index provider confirmed it will not alter existing rules to accommodate the company before its IPO.
cards.body:
S&P has rejected requests to change its rules that would have allowed SpaceX early entry into its benchmark index. The decision means the aerospace company will need to meet standard eligibility requirements before inclusion, despite the scale of its upcoming public offering.

The ruling affects how quickly institutional investors tied to S&P indexes will be able to purchase SpaceX shares. Index funds typically represent significant buying power for newly public companies, and delayed inclusion could impact early trading patterns after the IPO launches next week.

cards.headline: China builds economic barriers as global tensions increase
cards.teaser: Beijing is implementing changes it describes as necessary for national security.
cards.body:
China has introduced new economic measures that officials say are required for national security purposes. The changes could create complications for Chinese companies seeking growth opportunities in international markets.

The moves come as geopolitical tensions shape trade relationships between China and other major economies. The measures appear designed to increase domestic economic resilience but may limit Chinese firms' ability to expand overseas operations and partnerships.

cards.headline: Nvidia approves three major memory suppliers for HBM4 chips
cards.teaser: The graphics chip maker has selected its suppliers for next-generation high-bandwidth memory.
cards.body:
Nvidia has given approval to three major memory manufacturers to supply HBM4, the next generation of high-bandwidth memory used in advanced graphics processors. The announcement came from Nvidia's CEO.

The decision shapes the supply chain for future AI and graphics processing hardware. HBM4 represents a key component in high-performance computing applications, and supplier selection signals Nvidia's production plans for upcoming chip generations.

cards.headline: Anthropic calls for coordinated plan to halt AI development if risks escalate
cards.teaser: The AI research company says labs need the ability to pause work on advanced systems.
cards.body:
Anthropic has urged AI laboratories to create a coordinated mechanism for halting development if risks from artificial intelligence systems increase. Co-founder Jack Clark told the BBC that AI could reach a point where it develops without human input, describing the need for a brake pedal on the technology.

The company is advocating for a global framework that would allow AI labs to pause work collectively. Clark's comments highlight concerns within the AI industry about systems advancing beyond current safety measures and the need for coordinated action among competing research organizations.

cards.headline: China regulates content in viral micro drama industry
cards.teaser: Authorities are targeting material deemed to contain soft pornography, violence and materialism.
cards.body:
Chinese regulators have implemented a crackdown on micro dramas, short-form video content that has surged in popularity. The government is focusing on material it categorizes as containing soft pornography, violent content, and materialistic themes.

Micro dramas have become a major entertainment format in China but have drawn official criticism for sensationalist storytelling. The regulatory action affects content creators and platforms hosting the short videos, which have attracted large audiences through dramatic narratives condensed into brief episodes.

hero.headline: Microsoft AI chief criticizes Anthropic pricing as company unveils new developer tools
hero.body:
Microsoft's artificial intelligence leadership has publicly questioned the pricing of competing AI models from Anthropic, according to statements made during the company's Build 2026 conference. The criticism underscores intensifying competition in the commercial AI market, where cost has become a central point of differentiation among providers.

At Build 2026, Microsoft announced several new initiatives aimed at developers. The company repositioned Windows as a trusted development platform and revealed Project Solara, an Android-based operating system built specifically for AI agents rather than traditional applications. Microsoft also introduced new capabilities for developing agentic applications through Microsoft Fabric and Microsoft Databases, expanding its infrastructure offerings for AI-driven software.

The public criticism of Anthropic's pricing reflects broader competitive tensions in the AI industry. Companies are racing to capture market share while managing the substantial computational costs required to operate large language models. Anthropic has built a reputation around AI safety and technical capability, but faces increasing pressure to offer competitive pricing alongside its performance metrics. Microsoft, which maintains partnerships with OpenAI and has invested significantly in its own AI infrastructure, holds leverage to challenge competitor pricing strategies.

The Build conference highlighted Microsoft's renewed emphasis on Windows as a development platform, marking a strategic shift after years of prioritizing cloud services. Project Solara represents a novel approach to mobile operating systems, reimagining them around AI agents capable of taking actions on behalf of users without requiring direct app interaction.

Microsoft's pricing criticism emerges as Anthropic prepares for a potential initial public offering. The company announced in May that its annualized revenue had reached $47 billion, a dramatic increase from approximately $9 billion at the end of 2025. This growth trajectory demonstrates the rapid expansion of the commercial AI market, though it also faces questions about sustainable returns on AI investments.

The competitive dynamics suggest that cost efficiency will play a decisive role in determining which AI providers capture enterprise customers. Businesses evaluating AI deployments are increasingly focused not just on model capabilities but on total cost of ownership. As providers compete for large-scale commercial contracts, pricing strategies have moved from a secondary concern to a primary differentiator.

The timing of Microsoft's public comments reflects the high stakes in enterprise AI adoption. Companies want access to cutting-edge models, but they also need solutions that fit their budgets and operational requirements. Microsoft's emphasis on developer tools and platform reliability, combined with its criticism of competitor pricing, positions the company as offering both technical capability and economic advantage to organizations building AI applications at scale.

cards.headline: Anthropic reports revenue surge to $47 billion as IPO approaches
cards.teaser: The AI company announced annualized revenue crossed $47 billion in May, up sharply from $9 billion at the end of 2025.
cards.body:
Anthropic has disclosed that its annualized revenue exceeded $47 billion in May, representing growth from approximately $9 billion recorded at the end of 2025. The company's president Daniela Amodei addressed questions about returns on AI investments as the firm prepares for its initial public offering.

The revenue trajectory positions Anthropic among the fastest-growing AI companies as it moves toward going public. The sharp increase reflects growing enterprise adoption of the company's AI models, though the sustainability of that growth rate faces scrutiny from investors evaluating the economics of large language model businesses.

cards.headline: Airbnb CEO plans new artificial intelligence research lab
cards.teaser: Brian Chesky announced plans to launch an AI lab after previously saying existing language models weren't ready for partnership.
cards.body:
Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky announced plans to launch a new artificial intelligence laboratory. The move comes after Chesky previously stated that the company had not partnered with existing large language model providers because available products did not meet its needs.

The initiative reflects Airbnb's decision to develop its own AI capabilities tailored to the company's specific requirements rather than relying on third-party solutions currently available in the market.

cards.headline: Founders Fund produces game show featuring tech industry figures
cards.teaser: The venture capital firm launched a show starring Sam Altman, Palmer Luckey, and other technology leaders.
cards.body:
Founders Fund launched a game show featuring prominent technology industry figures, with the debut episode moderated by the firm's chief marketing officer Mike Solana. The cast included Sam Altman and Palmer Luckey alongside other current tech leaders.

The venture capital firm, known for early investments in Facebook and SpaceX, has ventured into entertainment content creation with the project, bringing together executives and entrepreneurs from its portfolio and the broader tech ecosystem.

cards.headline: Samsung to use dual chipset strategy for Galaxy Z Flip8
cards.teaser: The foldable phone will feature both Exynos and Snapdragon processors in different markets.
cards.body:
Samsung will equip the Galaxy Z Flip8 with both Exynos and Snapdragon processors, with the specific chip varying by region. This approach aligns with Samsung's strategy for its Galaxy S flagship lineup.

The dual-chipset plan allows Samsung to leverage its in-house Exynos processors while maintaining access to Qualcomm's Snapdragon technology across different markets. This flexibility helps Samsung manage production efficiency for its premium foldable devices.

cards.headline: Researchers identify tallest tree in East Asia after years of searching
cards.teaser: A Taiwania cryptomerioides nicknamed 'The Heaven Sword' stands 80 meters tall, earning the title after a nearly decade-long search.
cards.body:
Scientists have confirmed a Taiwania cryptomerioides tree known as 'The Heaven Sword' as the tallest tree in East Asia. The tree measures 80 meters in height and was identified after researchers conducted a search lasting nearly a decade.

The discovery represents the culmination of extensive fieldwork to locate and measure giant trees across the region. Taiwania cryptomerioides is a coniferous species native to East Asia, and this specimen's height establishes a new benchmark for tree height in the region. Researchers documented the finding through multiple measurement methods to confirm the record.

cards.headline: Mangrove forests recover after decades of decline
cards.teaser: Coastal mangrove ecosystems are making a comeback following years of human-caused destruction.
cards.body:
Mangrove forests are making a surprising comeback after experiencing widespread destruction from human activity. These swampy coastal ecosystems are expanding again across multiple regions around the world.

The recovery benefits both coastal communities and the climate. Mangrove forests shield shorelines from storm surges and erosion while sequestering substantial amounts of carbon. The turnaround reflects increased conservation efforts and reduced development pressure in some coastal areas where mangroves were previously cleared for agriculture, aquaculture, and urban development.

hero.headline: First-time Grand Slam champion to be crowned at French Open
hero.teaser: The men's semifinals in Paris will determine which player wins their first major title.
hero.body:
The French Open is guaranteed to crown a first-time Grand Slam champion this year after the men's and women's semifinals produced four players who have never won a major tournament.

In the men's draw, Flavio Cobolli reached the semifinals after a remarkable comeback victory. The Italian 10th seed defeated fourth-seeded Felix Auger-Aliassime 4-6, 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 in the quarterfinals, recovering from a set and a break down. This was Cobolli's first win against a top 10 opponent at a Grand Slam. His triumph set up an all-Italian men's semifinal for the first time in history, as Matteo Arnaldi also advanced when fellow Italian Matteo Berrettini retired injured.

Cobolli's path through the tournament has been efficient and authoritative. Through five matches, he has conceded just two sets while playing decisive tennis when it matters most. His game combines a destructive forehand with well-rounded skills that have allowed him to neutralize opponents' weapons. Against Auger-Aliassime, Cobolli pinned the Canadian in his backhand corner and narrowed the court with superior defensive abilities after breaking serve at 3-1 in the first set.

The loss represents a significant missed opportunity for Auger-Aliassime, who at 25 has been among the tour's longest-serving players without a major title. The Canadian was the highest-ranked player remaining in his half after Jannik Sinner's early exit, giving him a genuine chance to compete for the championship.

On the women's side, qualifier Maja Chwalinska reached the final with a stunning 7-6, 6-4 victory over 25th seed Diana Shnaider. Chwalinska became the first qualifier ever to reach a Roland Garros final. Her emotional response after the win, sobbing into her towel, reflected the magnitude of her achievement after coming through an extraordinarily difficult period in her life.

The pressure of competing for a first major title will test all four semifinalists in different ways. Cobolli and Arnaldi must navigate their historic matchup while maintaining the form that brought them this far. Chwalinska carries the weight of her journey and the expectations that come with being the first qualifier to reach this final. Her opponent in the women's final will also be pursuing their first Grand Slam title.

The absence of established champions in both semifinals means that Sunday's finals will feature players competing for major titles for the first time in their careers. How each handles the pressure and intensity of that moment could determine who leaves Roland Garros with their name etched into Grand Slam history.

cards.headline: Hurricanes defeat Golden Knights in overtime to tie Stanley Cup Final
cards.teaser: Carolina scored an overtime goal in Game 2 to even the Stanley Cup Final series against Vegas.
cards.body:
Seth Jarvis scored the game-winning goal 3:56 into overtime on a power play as the Carolina Hurricanes defeated the Vegas Golden Knights 4-3 in Game 2 of the Stanley Cup Final on Thursday night. The victory evened the series at one game apiece after Vegas won the opener.

The Hurricanes mounted an impressive comeback, erasing a two-goal deficit in the third period. The period proved dramatic, with four goals scored and another called back due to goaltender interference. The failed Vegas challenge ultimately proved costly, setting up the power play that led to Jarvis's overtime heroics.

cards.headline: Texas wins second consecutive Women's College World Series title
cards.teaser: The Longhorns defeated Texas Tech to claim back-to-back national championships, with Teagan Kavan earning Most Outstanding Player honors again.
cards.body:
Texas claimed back-to-back Women's College World Series championships on Thursday, defeating Texas Tech in the finals. The victory marks the Longhorns' second consecutive national title.

Teagan Kavan earned Most Outstanding Player honors for the second year running, capping off another dominant tournament performance for Texas softball.

cards.headline: Jennifer Kupcho leads US Women's Open after first round
cards.teaser: Kupcho shot the low round Thursday to take a one-stroke lead at golf's second women's major of the year.
cards.body:
Jennifer Kupcho made a strong start to the US Women's Open, golf's second women's major of the year, taking a one-shot lead after Thursday's first round. Her performance positioned her well as she heads into Friday's play.

The tournament is one of the most prestigious events in women's golf, with players competing for one of sport's most coveted titles over the remaining three rounds.

cards.headline: Caitlin Clark scores 17 as Fever defeat Dream
cards.teaser: Indiana's rookie guard recovered after vomiting at halftime to help lead the Fever past Atlanta.
cards.body:
Caitlin Clark scored 17 points as the Indiana Fever defeated the Atlanta Dream on Thursday. The rookie became ill during the game, vomiting at halftime, but returned to the court and contributed to the victory. Angel Reese played for the Dream in the matchup.

Clark tied her own WNBA record during the contest as the Fever moved past recent drama with the win. The game marked another chapter in the ongoing rookie storylines as both Clark and Reese continue their professional careers.

cards.headline: Kieran Morrison makes senior debut for Northern Ireland
cards.teaser: The Liverpool teenager appeared for his country against Guinea on Thursday.
cards.body:
Liverpool teenager Kieran Morrison made his senior debut for Northern Ireland against Guinea on Thursday. The midfielder expressed his excitement about earning his first cap for the national team.

Morrison received the news of his selection through a familiar phone call, marking a significant milestone as he steps up to international football at senior level.

cards.headline: Aaron Judge diagnosed with rib stress fracture, out at least four weeks
cards.teaser: New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge has been diagnosed with a stress fracture in his ribs on his right side and will be reevaluated in four to six weeks, th.
cards.body:
New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge has been diagnosed with a stress fracture on the right side of his rib cage. The team announced he will be reevaluated in four to six weeks, meaning he will miss at least a month of play.

The injury significantly impacts the Yankees' lineup during a competitive stretch of the season. Judge, a cornerstone of the team's offense, will be sidelined from baseball activities while the fracture heals. His absence creates a gap in both the batting order and outfield defense as the Yankees adjust their roster.

hero.headline: Actor James Handy Killed in Stabbing at His California Home
hero.body:
James Handy, a veteran character actor known for roles in Top Gun: Maverick and Jumanji, has died following a fatal stabbing at his home in Tarzana, California. The 81-year-old actor was found in the front yard of his residence at 9:30 a.m. on Wednesday with multiple stab wounds to the chest. He was unconscious when discovered.

The Los Angeles Police Department arrested Michael Gledhill, 44, the son of Handy's girlfriend, in connection with the killing. Gledhill has been charged on suspicion of murder, with bail set at $2 million.

According to police, a 911 caller stated: "I am the son of man, I just killed the man of sin." When officers arrived at the scene, Gledhill told them he was "the one they were looking for." Police confirmed that the suspect resides at the location with his mother, who is Handy's girlfriend.

Handy built a lengthy career as a character actor, frequently taking on authoritative and military roles. Beyond Top Gun: Maverick and Jumanji, his filmography includes appearances in Logan, K-911, and numerous television series including Law and Order, NCIS: Los Angeles, and Criminal Minds. His acting career began in 1977 on the television series Ryan's Hope. His most recent film role was in Top Gun: Maverick in 2022.

The New York-born actor became a recognizable presence in Hollywood across multiple decades, known for bringing gravitas to supporting roles. His experience and reliable performances made him a dependable choice for filmmakers seeking seasoned character actors to fill important parts in major productions.

The stabbing marks a tragic loss for the entertainment industry, where Handy maintained a steady working presence throughout his long career. Details about what led to the attack have not been disclosed by authorities. The investigation into the circumstances surrounding the killing remains ongoing.

cards.headline: CBS Correspondent Scott Pelley Fired After Confronting Network Leadership
cards.teaser: The longtime journalist was removed from 60 Minutes along with two other correspondents in a shakeup that has created upheaval at the news program.
cards.body:
Scott Pelley, a veteran 60 Minutes correspondent, was fired by CBS News after clashing with new management. He accused network executives of instructing him to inject falsehoods and bias into his reporting and of silencing employees.

Pelley stated that 60 Minutes built its decades-long success as America's top program through integrity, quality, and humanity in storytelling. Nick Bilton has taken over as the new chief of the program. Former correspondent Steve Kroft remarked that the 60 Minutes the public knew no longer exists.

cards.headline: Scary Movie Reboot Earns $7.5 Million in Thursday Previews
cards.teaser: The revived horror comedy franchise opened with preview numbers approaching those of Scream 7, while Masters of the Universe took in $4 million.
cards.body:
The new Scary Movie film earned $7.5 million in Thursday night previews, positioning it near the opening preview performance of Scream 7. The reboot brings back the Wayans Brothers to the slasher spoof franchise. Masters of the Universe collected $4 million in its Thursday night debut.

The Scary Movie series has historically relied on timing to succeed. The original film capitalized on the wave of slashers following Scream 3's 2000 release. This sixth installment, which drops the numbering like the first film, arrives as horror and spoofs continue to draw audiences.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift Releases Original Song for Toy Story 5
cards.teaser: The singer wrote and produced a track focused on the character Jessie for the upcoming Pixar sequel, working with frequent collaborator Jack Antonoff.
cards.body:
Taylor Swift has released an original song for Toy Story 5 titled "I Knew It, I Knew You." The track was co-written and produced by Swift alongside Jack Antonoff, her longtime creative collaborator. The song celebrates Jessie, the cowgirl character from the film.

Swift shared cover art for the single featuring her with naturally curly hair in a stripped-down aesthetic. The announcement generated social media responses from notable figures, including Brittany Mahomes, wife of NFL player Patrick Mahomes.

cards.headline: Phoebe Bridgers Performs Phone-Free Acoustic Show at Madison Square Garden
cards.teaser: The singer played an intimate concert for 18,000 fans who locked up their devices, debuting eight new songs during the special performance.
cards.body:
Phoebe Bridgers held a special acoustic concert at Madison Square Garden where attendees locked up their phones for the duration of the show. The artist addressed the crowd of roughly 18,000 people, even acknowledging the unusual experience of performing without devices in the audience.

During the performance, Bridgers debuted eight new songs. The phone-free format transformed the massive arena into a more intimate setting, allowing fans to experience the music without digital distractions.

cards.headline: Kate Winslet Surprises Young Blind Film Fan With Personal Call
cards.teaser: The Oscar-winning actress reached out to teenager Eryn, who traveled three hours for an accessible film screening due to lack of local options.
cards.body:
Oscar-winning actress Kate Winslet surprised teenage film fan Eryn with a personal phone call. Eryn, who has been blind since birth, had traveled three hours round-trip to attend a film screening because no accessible cinema exists in her local area.

Winslet's gesture acknowledged the significant barriers facing moviegoers with disabilities who must undertake considerable journeys to access screenings with proper accommodations. The surprise call delighted the dedicated young cinema enthusiast.

cards.headline: Florida Georgia Line Reunite With Surprise CMA Fest Performance
cards.teaser: Tyler Hubbard and Brian Kelley performed together at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, signaling a return for the duo that split in 2022.
cards.body:
Florida Georgia Line made a surprise appearance at CMA Fest, marking the first public reunion of Tyler Hubbard and Brian Kelley since their 2022 split. The country music duo performed at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, signaling they have reformed the act.

The unexpected appearance came without advance announcement, taking festival attendees by surprise. Florida Georgia Line had been one of country music's most successful duos before Hubbard and Kelley decided to pursue separate projects four years ago.

hero.headline: Senate Republicans defeat proposal to block Trump anti-weaponization fund
hero.teaser: The Senate rejected a Democratic amendment to prohibit the Justice Department from establishing a $1.8 billion fund during budget votes.
hero.body:
Senate Republicans on Thursday blocked a Democratic attempt to prevent the creation of a $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund, though the narrow vote revealed growing divisions within the president's own party.

Democratic Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer proposed language that would have barred the payouts as part of Republican-backed legislation to fund Trump's mass deportation campaign. The amendment failed 49-50 after a three-hour voting session that saw senators huddling on the chamber floor.

Three Republican senators broke ranks to support the amendment. Susan Collins of Maine, Dan Sullivan of Alaska, and Jon Husted of Ohio all voted with Democrats. All three represent seats that Democrats are targeting in the midterm elections. Husted faces particular pressure, trailing his Democratic challenger by eight points in a recent Fox News poll.

The fund proposal has sparked significant bipartisan concern. Trump's plan would issue financial settlements to people connected to the January 6 insurrection. Acting U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche told lawmakers earlier this week that the administration would not move forward with the fund. However, Schumer argued that a formal legal ban was necessary.

"Republicans are trusting the word of Todd Blanche, who built a career on lying," Schumer said. He pointed out that Trump had expressed his enthusiasm for the fund just the day before, calling it important. Schumer questioned whether Trump could resist using the fund for his own benefit.

Schumer proposed his amendment to a $70 billion bill funding immigration enforcement agencies through 2029. Republicans are using the budget reconciliation process to bypass Democratic filibuster rules and pass the legislation along party lines. This funding bill has been at the center of a major standoff between the parties since January, when Democrats refused to approve appropriations without reforms, leading to a 75-day partial shutdown of the Department of Homeland Security.

After Schumer's amendment failed, Republican Senator Thom Tillis proposed alternative language that would prevent payments from the anti-weaponization fund and redirect that money toward Justice Department fraud efforts. Tillis argued the move would eliminate an unpopular measure while funding important work.

"This bill is unpopular. This administration has said they're not moving forward with it. This is an opportunity for us to put it to bed and to also fund the fraud division, which I think is very important," Tillis said.

Democrats rejected Tillis's amendment, with Senator Jeff Merkley of Oregon calling it insufficient. "Taking one slush fund and eliminating it and creating a new slush fund still under the control of the attorney general is not the way to go," Merkley said.

Tillis's proposal also failed, receiving support from only 11 Republicans and three Democrats.

cards.headline: House committee approves $1.15 trillion defense bill after 14-hour debate
cards.teaser: The House Armed Services Committee passed the annual defense policy bill late Thursday, advancing the nearly $1.15 trillion measure to the full House after a ma.
cards.body:
The House Armed Services Committee passed the annual defense policy bill Thursday evening, advancing the $1.15 trillion National Defense Authorization Act to the full House following an intensive 14-hour markup session. The committee voted 44 members in favor after debating approximately 900 proposed amendments to the fiscal 2027 bill.

The NDAA sets military policy and spending priorities across weapons systems, personnel costs, and operational budgets. Congress has passed a defense authorization bill for over 60 consecutive years, typically with bipartisan support. The measure now goes to the full House for debate and votes before moving to the Senate, where it must be reconciled with a Senate version and signed by the president to become law.

cards.headline: FCC to review $3 billion school internet subsidy program over screen time concerns
cards.teaser: The agency will conduct a complete review of the E-Rate program that provides internet access funding for schools and libraries.
cards.body:
The Federal Communications Commission announced it will review a $3 billion annual program that subsidizes internet access for schools and libraries. FCC Chair Brendan Carr cited concerns about excessive screen time among children and its effects on their health as the reason for the review.

Carr announced the commission will conduct a complete review of the E-Rate program and release its findings. The program provides financial support to help schools and libraries obtain affordable internet access, serving as a major source of connectivity funding for educational institutions nationwide.

cards.headline: Senator Susan Collins casts 10,000th consecutive Senate vote
cards.teaser: The Maine Republican reached the milestone during budget reconciliation voting on Thursday night.
cards.body:
Senator Susan Collins cast her 10,000th consecutive Senate vote on Thursday night, voting for a Democratic motion to send the $70 billion budget reconciliation package back to the Judiciary Committee. Collins stood at her desk and announced her vote when the clerk called her name.

Collins has not missed a Senate vote throughout her tenure, maintaining a perfect attendance record for floor votes. The milestone came during an extended series of amendment votes on the budget reconciliation legislation.

cards.headline: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Haaland could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, who served as Interior Secretary in the Biden administration, won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor. She will advance to the general election in November.

If elected, Haaland would make history as the first female Native American governor in the United States. She previously served as a U.S. Representative from New Mexico before joining the Biden cabinet.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra advances to California governor runoff
cards.teaser: The former Health and Human Services Secretary won one of two spots in November's general election.
cards.body:
Former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra advanced to the general election in the race for California governor. Decision Desk HQ projected Becerra secured one of the two spots in November's election to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.

Fox News commentator Steve Hilton, who has Trump's backing, and billionaire Tom Steyer are currently competing for the second spot on the November ballot. California uses a top-two primary system where the leading candidates from any party advance to the general election regardless of party affiliation.

cards.headline: Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner denies allegations in New York Times report
cards.teaser: The Democratic candidate disputed claims from past girlfriends about his behavior, suggesting political motivation behind the timing.
cards.body:
Maine Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner rejected allegations in a New York Times report about his treatment of women, calling them "politically motivated." The article included claims of physical misconduct and offensive remarks from a Republican operative and past girlfriends.

Platner stated he has not considered withdrawing from the Senate primary race. He emphasized that he had not once thought about dropping out despite the published allegations.
